paper.title: Duplex microstructure enhanced mechanical property and underlined mechanism in Fe35MnxAl0.1C low-density steel
paper.paper_scope: Studies the effect of Al content (x = 4, 6, 8 and 10 wt%) on the initial microstructure, dislocation types/patterns, strain hardening behavior and mechanical properties of Fe-35Mn-xAl-0.1C low-density steels, revealing an edge-dislocation/dynamic-slip-band-refinement ductility-enhancing mechanism in the 8Al ferrite-based duplex steel.

alloys.description: Designed low-density steel with the lowest Al content; after solution treatment it is a single-phase FCC austenite (austenitic) lightweight steel.
alloys.alloys_notes: Nominal composition given in the Materials section (b0016) as Fe-35Mn-xAl-1C-0.1Nb-0.1V-1Mo-1W; the title/abstract give Fe-35Mn-xAl-0.1C, and Table 1 measured C is ~0.094 wt%. Measured composition (Table 1): Mn 33.92, Al 4.13, C 0.094, Nb 0.11, V 0.11, Mo 1.20, W 0.98 wt%. Density 7.42 g/cm3.

alloys.description: Designed low-density steel with 8 wt% Al; after solution treatment it is a ferrite-based duplex lightweight steel (75.7 % ferrite + 24.3 % austenite), showing the best strength-ductility balance.
alloys.alloys_notes: Nominal composition given as Fe-35Mn-xAl-1C-0.1Nb-0.1V-1Mo-1W in b0016; title/abstract give 0.1C. Measured composition (Table 1): Mn 34.56, Al 8.10, C 0.076, Nb 0.11, V 0.11, Mo 1.31, W 1.27 wt%. Density 6.99 g/cm3.

alloys.description: Designed low-density steel with the highest Al content (10 wt%); after solution treatment it is nearly a fully ferrite-phase steel (98.1 % ferrite) that exhibits brittle behaviour with only ~4.6 % elongation.
alloys.alloys_notes: Nominal composition given as Fe-35Mn-xAl-1C-0.1Nb-0.1V-1Mo-1W in b0016; title/abstract give 0.1C. Measured composition (Table 1): Mn 34.66, Al 10.17, C 0.097, Nb 0.11, V 0.11, Mo 1.30, W 1.38 wt%. Density 6.84 g/cm3. Contains acicular 18R martensite precipitates in ferrite.

source.reason: Fe35Mn10Al0.1C is explicitly one of the four designed compositions and is described as a ferrite-based duplex (nearly fully ferritic) lightweight steel, distinct from the 4/6/8Al steels.

processes.process_name: Solution treatment at 1050 °C for 2 h followed by oil quenching
processes.description: Cast ingots homogenized at 1150 °C for 4 h and hot-forged into 16.5 mm diameter rods, then solution-treated at 1050 °C for 2 h followed by oil quenching to obtain nearly equiaxed grains; this identical treatment is applied to all four (4/6/8/10Al) steels, which are hereafter referred to as the solution-treated 4Al, 6Al, 8Al and 10Al steels.
processes.processes_notes: The same solution-treatment route is shared by all four alloy compositions, so alloy_id is left null and this single process is combined with each alloy to form four samples. b0016 states oil quenching while b0022 refers to 'water-quenched steel rods'; the primary terminal state is the 1050 °C/2 h solution treatment followed by quenching.

source.reason: b0016 defines the full thermo-mechanical route (homogenization 1150 °C/4 h, hot forging, solution treatment 1050 °C/2 h, oil quenching) and states the four solution-treated steels are named 4Al/6Al/8Al/10Al; this terminal state is common to all alloys.
The 4Al (Fe-35Mn-4Al-0.1C) composition after the shared solution treatment at 1050 °C/2 h + quenching; reported as a single-phase FCC austenite steel.
The 6Al (Fe-35Mn-6Al-0.1C) composition after the shared solution treatment at 1050 °C/2 h + quenching; reported as an austenite-based duplex lightweight steel.
The 8Al (Fe-35Mn-8Al-0.1C) composition after the shared solution treatment at 1050 °C/2 h + quenching; reported as a ferrite-based duplex lightweight steel with excellent strength-ductility balance.
The 10Al (Fe-35Mn-10Al-0.1C) composition after the shared solution treatment at 1050 °C/2 h + quenching; reported as nearly a fully ferrite-phase steel that is brittle.

unmapped_findings: Nominal composition is written as Fe-35Mn-xAl-1C-0.1Nb-0.1V-1Mo-1W in the Materials section (b0016), whereas the title/abstract give Fe-35Mn-xAl-0.1C; measured C is ~0.076–0.097 wt% (Table 1, b0018).
Densities of the investigated steels measured by the Archimedes principle are 7.42, 7.18, 6.99 and 6.84 g/cm3 for 4Al, 6Al, 8Al and 10Al, respectively (b0016).
XRD mass fractions of ferrite are 75.7 % for 8Al and 98.1 % for 10Al steel (b0032).
Interrupted tensile tests were performed to engineering strains of 3 %, 10 %, 20 % and 28 % to study deformation-microstructure evolution (b0022, b0049).
Calculated austenite stacking fault energies at room temperature are 51.25, 62.64 and 68.47 mJ/m2 for 4Al, 6Al and 8Al austenite respectively (Table 2, b0029).
